---
title: "Run the Pipeline"
---

On Unity, the pipeline runs as a **SLURM batch job**, not interactively in the terminal. You write a shell script, submit it with `sbatch`, and SLURM runs it on a compute node while you can log out and do other things.

## Understanding the job script

A job script is a plain text file. It has two parts:

1. **`#SBATCH` lines at the top**, these tell SLURM how much time and memory to reserve, and where to write the output
2. **Shell commands below**, these are the actual commands that run

Here is what each `#SBATCH` line means:

```bash
#SBATCH --job-name=nfcore-rnaseq-test   # A label shown in the queue
#SBATCH --partition=cpu                  # Use CPU nodes (not GPU)
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8               # Reserve 8 CPU cores for the manager process
#SBATCH --mem=48G                        # Reserve 48 GB of RAM
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00                  # Maximum run time (hours:minutes:seconds)
#SBATCH --output=.../%j.out             # File for standard output (%j = job ID)
#SBATCH --error=.../%j.err              # File for error output
#SBATCH --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL      # Email you when the job starts, ends, or fails
#SBATCH --mail-user=you@email.edu       # Your email address
```

::: {.callout-note}
The `--cpus-per-task=8` and `--mem=48G` here are for the Nextflow manager process, not the individual pipeline steps. The pipeline itself will request additional resources for each step through SLURM automatically.
:::

## Understanding the environment setup

Inside the script, several lines set up the environment before running Nextflow:

```bash
module purge                         # Clear any previously loaded modules
module load nextflow/26.04.1         # Load Nextflow
module load apptainer/latest         # Load Apptainer (the container system)
```

The `export` lines tell Apptainer and Nextflow where to store container images and temporary files:

```bash
export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="..."      # Where Apptainer stores downloaded container images
export APPTAINER_TMPDIR="..."        # Temporary files during container builds
export NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="..."  # Where Nextflow looks for Apptainer images
export NXF_OPTS='-Xms1g -Xmx4g'    # Memory limits for the Nextflow Java process
export PROOT_NO_SECCOMP=1           # Required for Apptainer to work correctly on Unity
```

These variables must point to your scratch workspace so they do not fill up your home directory.

## Step 1: Run a test first

Before running with your own data, run the built-in test profile. This uses a tiny dataset that comes with the pipeline and confirms everything is working correctly on Unity.

### Create the script

On Unity, open a new file with nano:

```bash
nano ~/rnaseq_nf_core/nfcore-rnaseq-test.sh
```

Paste in the following. Replace `YOUR_USERNAME` with your Unity username and `YOUR_WORKSPACE` with your scratch workspace name (from `ws_list`):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=nfcore-rnaseq-test
#SBATCH --partition=cpu
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=48G
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00
#SBATCH --output=/home/YOUR_USERNAME/rnaseq_nf_core/job-logs/nfcore-rnaseq-test.%j.out
#SBATCH --error=/home/YOUR_USERNAME/rnaseq_nf_core/job-logs/nfcore-rnaseq-test.%j.err
#SBATCH --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL
#SBATCH --mail-user=you@email.edu

set -euo pipefail

SCRATCH_RNASEQ=/scratch4/workspace/YOUR_USERNAME-YOUR_WORKSPACE

cd "$SCRATCH_RNASEQ"

module purge
module load nextflow/26.04.1
module load apptainer/latest

mkdir -p "$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/.apptainer/build-cache"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/.apptainer/tmp"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/.nextflow-apptainer-cache"

export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/.apptainer/build-cache"
export APPTAINER_TMPDIR="$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/.apptainer/tmp"
export NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/.nextflow-apptainer-cache"
export NXF_OPTS='-Xms1g -Xmx4g'
export PROOT_NO_SECCOMP=1

# Remove any partial container downloads from a previous attempt
find "$NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR" -type f -name "*.pulling.*" -delete || true

nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq \
  -r 3.26.0 \
  -profile test,unity \
  --outdir test_results \
  -resume
```

Save and close nano: `Ctrl + O`, `Enter`, `Ctrl + X`.

### What the nextflow command means

```bash
nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq \   # Run the nf-core/rnaseq pipeline
  -r 3.26.0 \                   # Use version 3.26.0 (pin the version for reproducibility)
  -profile test,unity \          # Use the built-in test dataset AND Unity cluster settings
  --outdir test_results \        # Put all output in a folder called test_results
  -resume                        # Resume from cached steps if re-run
```

### Submit and monitor the job

```bash
sbatch ~/rnaseq_nf_core/nfcore-rnaseq-test.sh
```

You will see something like:

```text
Submitted batch job 12345678
```

Note the job ID, you will use it to check status or find your log files.

Check whether the job is running:

```bash
squeue --me
```

Watch the log file update in real time (replace `12345678` with your job ID):

```bash
tail -f ~/rnaseq_nf_core/job-logs/nfcore-rnaseq-test.12345678.out
```

Press `Ctrl + C` to stop watching.

::: {.callout-tip}
The test profile uses a small built-in dataset. It can take a few hours because the first run needs to download Apptainer container images. Subsequent runs are faster because the containers are cached.
:::

### How to tell if the test succeeded

A successful test run ends with something like:

```text
-[nf-core/rnaseq] Pipeline completed successfully -
```

If you see `Pipeline completed with errors`, check the `.err` log file for details.

## Step 2: Run with all of the lab's samples

The real run uses one SLURM script that does everything itself:

1. Checks that the input folders, genome files, and shared container cache exist
2. **Builds the samplesheet automatically** from every FASTQ pair in both sequencing folders
3. Writes the params JSON file
4. Checks that the shared container images are valid
5. Launches nf-core/rnaseq

You do not write the samplesheet or params file by hand, the script regenerates both every time it runs.

### What the run uses

| Input | Path on Unity |
|---|---|
| FASTQ folder 1 (first sequencing run) | `/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/03_26_flut_yale_rnaseq_raw` |
| FASTQ folder 2 (replication run) | `/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/08_26_flut_yale_rnaseq_replication_raw` |
| Reference genome folder | `/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/ncbi_reference_genome_10_26` |
| Genome FASTA | `GCF_062004578.1_SC_StPar_1.0_genomic.fna` |
| Genome GTF | `GCF_062004578.1_SC_StPar_1.0_genomic.gtf` |
| Shared container cache | `/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/nfcore_container_cache/rnaseq-3.26.0` |

The reference is the NCBI RefSeq assembly **GCF_062004578.1 (SC_StPar_1.0)** with annotation release **GCF_062004578.1-RS_2026_10**. See [Frog Data Availability](frog-data-availability.qmd) for more on these files.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why a shared container cache?
The lab keeps one copy of every Apptainer image that nf-core/rnaseq 3.26.0 needs in `/work/`. Pointing `NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR` there means your run does not have to download and build the containers again, which saves hours and avoids most container errors. If the script reports an invalid image, ask whoever maintains the cache to rebuild it rather than deleting files yourself.
:::

### Create the script

Make a folder for your scripts, then open a new file:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/rnaseq_nf_core/scripts ~/rnaseq_nf_core/job-logs
nano ~/rnaseq_nf_core/scripts/run-nfcore.sh
```

Paste in the script below. Replace `YOUR_USERNAME` with your Unity username, `/scratch3/workspace/YOUR_USERNAME-YOUR_WORKSPACE` with your scratch workspace path (from `ws_list`), and `you@email.edu` with your email:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=nfcore-rnaseq-ncbi-ref
#SBATCH --partition=cpu
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=48G
#SBATCH --time=3-00:00:00
#SBATCH --output=/home/YOUR_USERNAME/rnaseq_nf_core/job-logs/nfcore-ncbi-ref.%j.out
#SBATCH --error=/home/YOUR_USERNAME/rnaseq_nf_core/job-logs/nfcore-ncbi-ref.%j.err
#SBATCH --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL
#SBATCH --mail-user=you@email.edu

set -euo pipefail

SCRATCH_RNASEQ=/scratch3/workspace/YOUR_USERNAME-YOUR_WORKSPACE
SHARED_CONTAINER_CACHE=/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/nfcore_container_cache/rnaseq-3.26.0

# Samples come from both sequencing runs
FASTQ_DIR_1=/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/03_26_flut_yale_rnaseq_raw
FASTQ_DIR_2=/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/08_26_flut_yale_rnaseq_replication_raw

# NCBI RefSeq reference: GCF_062004578.1 (SC_StPar_1.0), annotation GCF_062004578.1-RS_2026_10
GENOME_DIR=/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/ncbi_reference_genome_10_26
GENOME_FASTA="$GENOME_DIR/GCF_062004578.1_SC_StPar_1.0_genomic.fna"
GENOME_GTF="$GENOME_DIR/GCF_062004578.1_SC_StPar_1.0_genomic.gtf"

SAMPLESHEET="/home/YOUR_USERNAME/rnaseq_nf_core/scripts/samplesheet.csv"
PARAMS="/home/YOUR_USERNAME/rnaseq_nf_core/scripts/ncbi_ref_all_samples_params.json"

OUTDIR="$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/results_all_samples_ncbi_ref"

echo "Running on host: $(hostname)"
echo "Started at: $(date)"
echo "Scratch workspace: $SCRATCH_RNASEQ"
echo "Shared container cache: $SHARED_CONTAINER_CACHE"
echo "FASTQ directory 1: $FASTQ_DIR_1"
echo "FASTQ directory 2: $FASTQ_DIR_2"
echo "Genome FASTA: $GENOME_FASTA"
echo "Genome GTF: $GENOME_GTF"
echo "Output directory: $OUTDIR"

cd "$SCRATCH_RNASEQ"

module purge
module load nextflow/26.04.1
module load apptainer/latest

mkdir -p "$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/.apptainer/build-cache"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/.apptainer/tmp"
mkdir -p /home/YOUR_USERNAME/rnaseq_nf_core/job-logs
mkdir -p /home/YOUR_USERNAME/rnaseq_nf_core/scripts

export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/.apptainer/build-cache"
export APPTAINER_TMPDIR="$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/.apptainer/tmp"
export PROOT_TMP_DIR="$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/.apptainer/tmp"
export TMPDIR="$SCRATCH_RNASEQ/.apptainer/tmp"
export NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR="$SHARED_CONTAINER_CACHE"
export NXF_OPTS='-Xms1g -Xmx4g'
export PROOT_NO_SECCOMP=1

echo "Checking required directories..."
for d in "$SCRATCH_RNASEQ" "$FASTQ_DIR_1" "$FASTQ_DIR_2" "$GENOME_DIR" "$SHARED_CONTAINER_CACHE"; do
    if [[ ! -d "$d" ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: Missing directory: $d"
        exit 1
    fi
done

echo "Checking genome files..."
for f in "$GENOME_FASTA" "$GENOME_GTF"; do
    if [[ ! -s "$f" ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: Missing or empty genome file: $f"
        exit 1
    fi
done

echo "Writing samplesheet from all FASTQ pairs..."
echo "sample,fastq_1,fastq_2,strandedness" > "$SAMPLESHEET"

shopt -s nullglob
r1_files=("$FASTQ_DIR_1"/*_R1_001.fastq.gz "$FASTQ_DIR_2"/*_R1_001.fastq.gz)

if [[ ${#r1_files[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: No R1 FASTQ files found in $FASTQ_DIR_1 or $FASTQ_DIR_2"
    exit 1
fi

for r1 in "${r1_files[@]}"; do
    dir=$(dirname "$r1")
    sample=$(basename "$r1" _R1_001.fastq.gz)
    r2="$dir/${sample}_R2_001.fastq.gz"

    if [[ ! -s "$r2" ]]; then
        echo "ERROR: Missing R2 for sample $sample: $r2"
        exit 1
    fi

    echo "${sample},${r1},${r2},auto" >> "$SAMPLESHEET"
done

echo "Samplesheet:"
cat "$SAMPLESHEET"

echo "Number of samples:"
tail -n +2 "$SAMPLESHEET" | wc -l

echo "Writing params file..."
cat > "$PARAMS" <<EOF
{
  "input": "$SAMPLESHEET",
  "outdir": "$OUTDIR",
  "fasta": "$GENOME_FASTA",
  "gtf": "$GENOME_GTF",
  "igenomes_ignore": true,
  "aligner": "star_salmon",
  "pseudo_aligner": "salmon",
  "gtf_extra_attributes": "gene",
  "featurecounts_group_type": "transcript_biotype",
  "save_reference": true,
  "max_cpus": 48,
  "max_memory": "256.GB",
  "max_time": "72.h"
}
EOF

echo "Checking shared Apptainer images..."
find "$NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR" -type f -name "*.img" | while read -r img; do
    if ! apptainer inspect "$img" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "ERROR: Invalid shared container image: $img"
        echo "Ask the cache owner to rebuild the shared cache."
        exit 1
    fi
done

echo "Nextflow version:"
nextflow -version

echo "Apptainer version:"
apptainer --version

echo "Launching nf-core/rnaseq with all samples and NCBI RefSeq genome GCF_062004578.1..."
nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq \
  -r 3.26.0 \
  -profile unity \
  -params-file "$PARAMS" \
  -resume

echo "Finished at: $(date)"
```

Save and close nano: `Ctrl + O`, `Enter`, `Ctrl + X`.

::: {.callout-important}
Use your own scratch workspace for `SCRATCH_RNASEQ`. Your workspace may be on `/scratch3` or `/scratch4`, copy the exact path from `ws_list`.
:::

### What each part of the script does

**Pre-flight checks.** Before anything runs, the script confirms that every folder exists and that the genome FASTA and GTF are not empty. If something is missing, the job stops right away with a clear `ERROR:` message in the `.out` log, instead of failing hours later inside Nextflow.

**Building the samplesheet.** The script finds every file ending in `_R1_001.fastq.gz` in both FASTQ folders. For each one it:

- Uses the file name without `_R1_001.fastq.gz` as the sample name (for example `C45-1B_S2_L002`)
- Finds the matching `_R2_001.fastq.gz` file in the same folder, and stops with an error if it is missing
- Writes one row to `samplesheet.csv`

The resulting samplesheet looks like this:

```text
sample,fastq_1,fastq_2,strandedness
C45-1B_S2_L002,/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/03_26_flut_yale_rnaseq_raw/C45-1B_S2_L002_R1_001.fastq.gz,/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/03_26_flut_yale_rnaseq_raw/C45-1B_S2_L002_R2_001.fastq.gz,auto
C45-1H_S1_L002,/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/03_26_flut_yale_rnaseq_raw/C45-1H_S1_L002_R1_001.fastq.gz,/work/pi_lmangiamele_smith_edu/03_26_flut_yale_rnaseq_raw/C45-1H_S1_L002_R2_001.fastq.gz,auto
...
```

| Column | What it contains |
|---|---|
| `sample` | Sample name taken from the FASTQ file name |
| `fastq_1` | Full path to the R1 (forward) FASTQ file |
| `fastq_2` | Full path to the R2 (reverse) FASTQ file |
| `strandedness` | `auto`, the pipeline subsamples reads and uses Salmon to detect the library strandedness for each sample |

The job log prints the full samplesheet and the number of samples, check these first to make sure every sample was picked up.

::: {.callout-tip}
If two rows have the same `sample` name, nf-core/rnaseq treats them as technical replicates and merges their reads. Because the sample names here include the `_S#_L00#` suffix, rows from the two sequencing runs stay separate unless the file names are identical.
:::

**Writing the params file.** The script writes the pipeline options to a JSON file. Using a JSON file avoids errors where `true`/`false` values passed on the command line are read as text.

| Parameter | What it does |
|---|---|
| `input` | The samplesheet the script just wrote |
| `outdir` | Where results go, inside your scratch workspace |
| `fasta`, `gtf` | The NCBI RefSeq genome and annotation |
| `igenomes_ignore` | Do not use nf-core's built-in reference genomes (there is none for *S. parvus*) |
| `aligner` | `star_salmon`, align reads to the genome with STAR, then quantify with Salmon |
| `pseudo_aligner` | Also run Salmon directly on the reads as a fast pseudo-alignment |
| `gtf_extra_attributes` | Carry the GTF `gene` attribute (gene symbols) into the count tables |
| `featurecounts_group_type` | Summarise biotype QC by the GTF's `transcript_biotype` attribute |
| `save_reference` | Save the STAR and Salmon indexes it builds, so they can be reused |
| `max_cpus`, `max_memory`, `max_time` | Upper limits on what any single pipeline step can request |

**Checking the shared containers.** The script runs `apptainer inspect` on every image in the shared cache. If any image is corrupt, the job stops and tells you which one. Do not delete images from the shared cache yourself, other lab members use it too.

**Launching the pipeline.** The final `nextflow run` command is the same as in the test run, except it uses `-profile unity` (no `test`) and reads all options from the params file.

### Submit

```bash
sbatch ~/rnaseq_nf_core/scripts/run-nfcore.sh
```

Then watch the log (replace `12345678` with your job ID):

```bash
tail -f ~/rnaseq_nf_core/job-logs/nfcore-ncbi-ref.12345678.out
```

The first lines show the paths, the generated samplesheet, and the sample count. If any check fails you will see a line starting with `ERROR:` and the job will end.

::: {.callout-note}
With all samples, the run takes many hours to a few days. The script reserves up to 3 days (`--time=3-00:00:00`). If it runs out of time, resubmit the same script, `-resume` will pick up where it stopped.
:::

## Checking on a running job

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| See your jobs in the queue | `squeue --me` |
| Watch the output log live | `tail -f ~/rnaseq_nf_core/job-logs/nfcore-ncbi-ref.JOBID.out` |
| Watch the error log live | `tail -f ~/rnaseq_nf_core/job-logs/nfcore-ncbi-ref.JOBID.err` |
| Cancel a job | `scancel JOBID` |

Replace `JOBID` with the number that `sbatch` printed when you submitted.

## Resuming an interrupted run

If your job ran out of time or failed partway through, fix the problem and resubmit with the same script. The `-resume` flag is already included, Nextflow will skip steps that finished successfully and continue from where it stopped.

::: {.callout-warning}
Only resume using the same scratch directory and the same params file. Changing the output path or key parameters invalidates the cached steps and forces a full restart.
:::

## Record keeping

Keep a copy of your SLURM script, the generated `samplesheet.csv`, and the params JSON alongside your final results. The `pipeline_info/` folder inside the results directory also stores exact parameters, software versions, and execution logs automatically.
